audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Drafted from supplied Hebrew witnesses; preserves YHWH rendering and literal military numbers where Hebrew reads 'thousand thousands' and place-name variants; needs witness review for numerals and some place-name readings.

verses.restored: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land had rest ten years.

familiar.text: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land was quiet ten years.

verses.restored: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of YHWH his God.

familiar.text: And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God:

verses.restored: For he removed the altars of the foreign gods and the high places, broke down the standing stones, and cut down the Asherah poles.

familiar.text: For he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves:

verses.restored: He commanded Judah to seek YHWH, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.

familiar.text: And commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.

verses.restored: Also he removed from all the cities of Judah the high places and the standing stones; and the kingdom was quiet before him.

familiar.text: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.

verses.restored: He built fortified towns in Judah, for the land had rest and there was no war in those years; for YHWH had given him rest.

familiar.text: And he built fenced cities in Judah: for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because the LORD had given him rest.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Repeated verb 'we sought' in following clause in Hebrew emphasizes communal seeking as cause of rest (v.7).

verses.restored: Therefore he said to Judah, 'Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with gates and bars; for the land is still before us — because we have sought YHWH our God, we sought him, and he has given us rest on every side.' So they built and prospered.

familiar.text: Therefore he said unto Judah, Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the LORD our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.

verses.restored: Asa had an army that bore shield and spear — out of Judah three hundred thousand; and out of Benjamin men who bore shields and drew bows two hundred and eighty thousand — all these were mighty men of valour.

familiar.text: And Asa had an army of men that bare targets and spears, out of Judah three hundred thousand; and out of Benjamin, that bare shields and drew bows, two hundred and fourscore thousand: all these were mighty men of valour.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew military totals are large; the following verse (v.9) reads 'thousand thousands' — magnitude is debated in the witnesses.

verses.restored: And there came out against them Zerah the Cushite with a host of a thousand thousands and three hundred chariots; and he came to Mareshah.

familiar.text: And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew כּוּשׁ (Cush) rendered 'Cushite'; 'thousand thousands' preserved literally; both require witness comparison.

verses.restored: Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah by Mareshah.

familiar.text: Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

verses.restored: And Asa cried to YHWH his God, and said, 'YHWH, there is nothing too hard for you to help, whether by many or by those of no power; help us, YHWH our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we come against this multitude. YHWH, you are our God; do not let man prevail against you.'

familiar.text: And Asa cried unto the LORD his God, and said, LORD, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O LORD our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O LORD, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.

verses.restored: So YHWH struck the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

familiar.text: So the LORD smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.

verses.restored: And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Gerar; and the Cushites were overthrown so that not one escaped alive, for they were crushed before YHWH and his host; and they carried away much spoil.

familiar.text: And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them unto Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the LORD, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.

verses.restored: They struck all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of YHWH fell upon them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was very much spoil in them.

familiar.text: And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the LORD came upon them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.

verses.restored: They also struck the cattle camps and took sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.

translation_notes: Divine name rendered as YHWH (Hebrew יהוה) throughout per project rule.
Numeric expressions follow the Hebrew wording (e.g., 'thousand thousands'); large-magnitude reading flagged for witness review.
Place-names (Mareshah, Zephathah/Gēi Zephathah) preserved; orthography reflects Hebrew forms.
safety_note: This chapter contains preserved descriptions of warfare and plunder; material retained for fidelity to source.
source_witness_audit_flags: numeric-magnitude: 'thousand thousands' (v.8) — confirm MT vs. alternatives
